newsitem.title: USA: Dlr ends on weak note ahead of US holiday weekend.
newsitem.headline: Dlr ends on weak note ahead of US holiday weekend.

text.p: The dollar fell against other major currencies on Thursday as hopes for a near-term increase in U.S. interest rates faded and traders locked in profits ahead of the long Independence Day weekend.
The dollar's losses were most pronounced against the pound, which rose sharply for a second consecutive day in anticipation of higher British rates.
Expectations for higher U.S. rates dwindled somewhat after the U.S. Labor Department's report on June employment showed an uptick in the U.S. unemployment rate to 5.0 percent from 4.8 percent in May.

The data appeared to validate the Federal Reserve's decision to keep interest rates steady after its policy meeting on Wednesday and suggested the economy may not require another rate hike in the coming months to slow it down and avert inflation.

"There is a shift toward the idea that the Fed is not going to move in August or even in September and if that's the case it takes away one of the dollar's main pillars of support," said Bob Savage, chief foreign exchange dealer at Lehman Brothers.

At 1500 EDT/1900 GMT, as trading ground to a halt ahead of the long weekend, the dollar stood at 113.77/87 yen, down from 114.31/36 at the open. It settled at 1.7530/40 marks, just below its opening rate of 1.7535/45.

The dollar pushed to its fourth consecutive 40-month high against the mark in overseas trade, but fell back when dealers saw the rise as an opportunity to book profits ahead of the holiday weekend in the U.S.
"A lot of traders in New York decided to square their positions and call it an early day," said Frank Pusateri, vice president of corporate foreign exchange at Mellon Bank.
Dollar losses against the German currency were well contained, in part due to a report showing a sharp 0.8 percent decline in German manufacturing orders for the month of May.
Broad mark weakness against the yen and the British pound also helped keep dollar losses against the mark to a minimum.

The pound rose to its highest level in almost six years against the mark and surged to a high of $1.6929, its top level since early January, before settling at $1.6910/20, up from $1.6755/65 at the open.

British Chancellor of the Exchequer Gordon Brown said on Thursday that he believed his budget had done what was necessary to bring fiscal and monetary policy back into balance and alleviate pressure on British exporters from the pound's steady rise.
But the market refused to cooperate, pushing the pound higher in anticipation of an interest hike from the Bank of England as early as next week.
"We saw a continuation of Wednesday's rally in sterling on the expectation of higher interest rates in Britain," said Ben Strauss, assistant vice president at Bank Julius Baer.
In other trade on Thursday, the dollar fell to 1.4687/97 Swiss francs from an opening rate of 1.4705/15. The dollar also fell to Canadian $1.3733/38 from C$1.3774/79.
